components.name: React SPA
components.runtime: User's browser. Dev: Vite on :5173 proxying /api to :8000. Prod: static files served by FastAPI.
components.responsibility: Chat UI: pick or upload a policy, ask questions, render verdict cards, cited quotes, cost breakdown, retrieved sources and the per-request trace.
components.inputs: User clicks/typing; JSON + Server-Sent Events from the API.
components.outputs: HTTP requests to /api/*; links that open the PDF at #page=N.

components.name: HTTP API layer
components.runtime: uvicorn worker process (single process; sync handlers run in the AnyIO thread pool).
components.responsibility: Routes, request validation, per-IP rate limits, upload checks, SSE streaming of /ask, assembling the trace, static frontend mount, CORS.

components.name: Composition root & settings
components.runtime: In-process; built once in the FastAPI lifespan and stored on app.state.services.
components.responsibility: Builds and holds long-lived objects (store, registry, retriever, LLM adapter, limiters). Reads all configuration from env / backend/.env via pydantic-settings. Startup indexing.

components.name: Ingestion & clause graph
components.runtime: In-process, synchronously inside the upload request and at startup.
components.responsibility: PDF → cleaned per-page text → injection lines stripped → section-aware chunks → cross-reference edges → two vectors per chunk in Qdrant. Federal Markdown → chunks.
components.inputs: PDF bytes on disk; Markdown files.
components.outputs: Chunks upserted into Qdrant; IndexedPolicy summary.

components.name: Retrieval pipeline
components.runtime: In-process; CPU-bound ONNX inference for embeddings and reranking.
components.responsibility: Lay-term query expansion → hybrid dense+BM25 search fused with RRF (per document, policy and federal separately) → cross-encoder rerank → relevance gate → one-hop clause-graph expansion.
components.outputs: RetrievalResult (ranked chunks, scores, timings, gate decision).

components.name: Answering & verification
components.runtime: In-process; blocks on the LLM HTTP call.
components.responsibility: Builds the tagged prompt, calls the LLM with a JSON schema, verifies quotes against source text, applies conflict downgrade and output guards, computes cost estimates in Python, extracts plan facts on upload.

components.name: LLM provider adapter
components.runtime: In-process client; outbound HTTPS to the provider.
components.responsibility: One interface (generate(system, user, schema)) with Gemini (default; model fallback chain) and Anthropic implementations; maps provider failures to user-safe LLMError; fills trace metadata.
components.inputs: System prompt, user message, Pydantic schema.

components.name: Security guards & abuse limits
components.runtime: In-process functions; limiter state in process memory.
components.responsibility: Ingestion-time injection scanner, output guards (markup stripping, unsupported contact redaction), plan-fact grounding, per-IP sliding-window limits, global daily LLM budget, safe document IDs.
components.inputs: Document text, model output, client IP.

components.name: Document registry (JSON files)
components.runtime: Local disk: backend/storage/uploads/ (git-ignored).
components.responsibility: One JSON metadata file + one PDF per document; 24-hour expiry for uploads; the sample is re-registered at every startup.

components.name: Qdrant vector store
components.runtime: Embedded on-disk mode (backend/storage/qdrant) unless QDRANT_URL is set; tests/evals use :memory:.
components.responsibility: Collection 'chunks': a 384-dim cosine dense vector + an IDF sparse (BM25) vector per chunk, payload with metadata, filtered hybrid queries with RRF fusion.

components.name: Local ONNX models (fastembed)
components.runtime: Loaded into process memory; files cached in backend/.cache/models (downloaded once, baked into the Docker image).
components.responsibility: bge-small dense embeddings, BM25 sparse vectors, ms-marco-MiniLM cross-encoder reranker.

components.name: Bundled knowledge (federal rules + sample policy)
components.runtime: Checked into backend/data/; read at startup.
components.responsibility: 11 Markdown summaries of US federal rules with source URLs; a fictional sample policy PDF and its hand-written plan facts.
components.outputs: Files read by the indexer and the composition root.

components.name: Google Gemini API
components.runtime: Remote (Google). Default provider when GEMINI_API_KEY is set.
components.responsibility: Structured-output generation for answers and plan-facts extraction. Free tier: per-model quotas and frequent 503/504 overload.

components.name: Anthropic Claude API (optional)
components.runtime: Remote. Used only if LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic or only ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set.
components.responsibility: Alternative provider via the Anthropic SDK beta parse() with server-side refusal fallbacks.
components.notes: Code path is unit-tested with a fake client only; every recorded eval/red-team run used Gemini, so live behaviour is unverified.

components.name: Hugging Face Hub (model downloads)
components.runtime: Remote; contacted by fastembed when models are loaded.
components.responsibility: Source of the ONNX model files. Local server logs show metadata requests to huggingface.co during startup even with a warm cache; whether the Docker image can start fully offline was not tested.

components.name: Evaluation harness
components.runtime: Developer machine; in-memory Qdrant; live LLM for the answer eval.
components.responsibility: Retrieval metrics (hit@k, MRR, gate sweep), multi-hop graph on/off comparison, end-to-end verdict/citation scoring with JSON result files.

components.name: Red-team attack suite
components.runtime: Developer machine; real FastAPI app via TestClient, in-memory Qdrant, live LLM.
components.responsibility: 11 OWASP-LLM-mapped attacks (hostile PDFs + hostile questions), 3 trials each, results saved as JSON.

components.name: Unit & API tests (pytest)
components.runtime: CI and developer machine; offline (fake embedder, fake LLM, in-memory Qdrant).
components.responsibility: Behavioural tests for every backend module and the full HTTP flow.

components.name: GitHub Actions CI
components.runtime: GitHub-hosted runners on push to main and on pull requests.
components.responsibility: Backend: pip install + pytest. Frontend: npm ci, lint, build. No deployment step.

components.name: Docker image
components.runtime: Multi-stage: node:22-alpine builds the SPA; python:3.12-slim runs uvicorn as non-root uid 1000 on $PORT (default 7860).
components.responsibility: Single deployable unit serving API + UI, with embedding models baked in.

flows.name: Application startup
flows.summary: uvicorn imports app.main, which builds the FastAPI app; the lifespan builds the Services container, indexes the federal corpus and the sample policy (skipped when the content hash is unchanged), deletes expired uploads, and warms up the ONNX models before serving.

steps.text: Import app.main: logging configured, `app = create_app()` registers CORS, the /api router and (if frontend/dist exists) StaticFiles at /.
Lifespan: build_services(get_settings()) creates Embedder, VectorStore (embedded Qdrant unless QDRANT_URL), DocumentRegistry, Retriever, limiters.
build_llm picks the provider from LLM_PROVIDER or whichever key exists; returns None when no key (answers disabled, retrieval still works).
ensure_collection creates 'chunks' (dense 384 cosine + sparse IDF) and keyword payload indexes if missing.
index_federal_corpus: hash all federal *.md (plus PIPELINE_VERSION); re-embed only if the stored version/count differ.
_register_sample: index the sample PDF with skip_if_current=True, then (re)write its DocumentRecord with facts from the checked-in JSON.
On change: delete all points for the doc_id, upsert new chunks with vectors.
delete_expired_uploads: remove uploads older than UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS from Qdrant and disk.
warm_up loads dense, sparse and reranker models so the first user request isn't slow.

flows.failure_notes: Any exception in the lifespan aborts startup (no retry). Startup work runs synchronously inside the async lifespan, so the server accepts no requests until indexing finishes.

flows.name: Ask a question (successful answer)
flows.summary: The most important path: browser POSTs /api/ask, the server streams status → sources → answer → done over SSE. Retrieval and the LLM call happen inside the streaming generator, so the client sees sources before the answer.

steps.text: ask(question) appends a 'loading' turn and calls askQuestion with an AbortController.
POST /api/ask {question, doc_id}; body validated by AskRequest (question 3-500 chars).
validate_doc_id → 404; registry lookup → 404; per-IP sliding window → 429 with Retry-After. All before streaming starts.
event: status 'Searching your policy...'
retrieve(question, doc_id): expand_query appends insurance terms for lay words.
embed_query: dense (bge-small query embedding) + sparse BM25 query vector.
hybrid_search twice: policy chunks of this doc_id (12) and federal chunks (6); each is a Qdrant query with two prefetches fused by RRF.
Cross-encoder reranks all candidates (slowest step on CPU).
Relevance gate: best score < GATE_THRESHOLD (-6) → empty result. Otherwise top-6 policy chunks.
Clause graph: follow refs of the top chunks one hop (≤3), fetched by id with retrieve().
event: sources (previews of every chunk the model will see, with linked_from).
No LLM configured → error event; daily budget exhausted → error event.
AnswerService.answer: build_user_message wraps excerpts in escaped <excerpt> tags + closing reminder.
generate(schema=LLMAnswer): JSON mode + response_json_schema + thinking level.
generate_content per model in [primary, fallbacks]; 429/5xx/timeouts move to the next model.
_parse checks finish reason (SAFETY/MAX_TOKENS) and validates JSON against the schema.
verify_citations (quote must match excerpt), conflict downgrade, strip_markup + redact_unsupported_contacts on every text field, compute_cost in Python, build trace.
event: answer (Answer.model_dump incl. trace), then event: done.
dispatch() parses each SSE block and calls onStatus/onSources/onAnswer/onError; AnswerCard + TracePanel render.

flows.failure_notes: Errors after streaming starts can't change the HTTP status (already 200); they're sent as `event: error`. AnswerError → its user-safe message; any other exception → generic message + log.exception.

flows.name: Off-topic question (relevance gate, no LLM call)
flows.summary: If the best reranked score is below GATE_THRESHOLD, retrieval returns no chunks and the API answers with a canned not_in_policy response. No LLM call, no budget spent.

steps.text: Search + rerank as usual.
best < gate → RetrievalResult with empty policy/federal, gate_passed=False.
found_anything is False → fallback_answer(), trace.llm = None.

flows.failure_notes: Calibration: gate value chosen from the sweep in eval/run_retrieval_eval.py (30/30 in-scope kept, 3/4 off-topic blocked).

flows.name: Upload a policy PDF (main write path)
flows.summary: Synchronous: the request returns only after the PDF is validated, sanitized, chunked, embedded and stored, and plan facts were extracted with one LLM call.

steps.text: handleFile → uploadDocument: multipart POST /api/documents.
Upload rate limit (429); read at most MAX_UPLOAD_MB+1 bytes (413); bytes must start with %PDF- (415).
delete_expired_uploads, then write storage/uploads/<uuid4 hex>.pdf.
index_policy_pdf → load_policy_pages: pypdf text per page, page/char caps (PdfLoadError → 422, file deleted).
strip_injection removes instruction-like lines per page; findings kept.
chunk_pages (section-aware, never crosses pages) then link_chunks builds cross-reference edges into chunk.extra['refs'].
_replace: delete by doc_id then upsert in batches of 64 (embeddings computed here).
If an LLM is configured AND the daily budget allows: extract_plan_facts on the sanitized pages (effort low).

evidence.match: svc\.llm is not None and svc\.daily_budget\.try_spend\(\)

steps.text: ground_plan_facts nulls numbers not literally present in the text and inconsistent pairs.
Save DocumentRecord JSON (with security_flags); return record.public() with 201.

flows.failure_notes: If embedding/upsert fails after the PDF was written, the PDF and any partially upserted points are not cleaned up (no try/except around those steps) - see finding rel:partial-upload. Plan-facts failures are non-fatal (facts=None).

flows.name: Open a cited page (representative read)
flows.summary: Citation links point at /api/documents/{id}/file#page=N; the server streams the PDF from the path stored in the registry, inline so the browser's PDF viewer jumps to the page.

steps.text: GET /api/documents/{doc_id}/file (browser navigation, new tab).
registry.get: invalid id → None (404); missing JSON → 404.
FileResponse(record.pdf_path, inline). The path comes from server-written JSON, never from the request.

flows.failure_notes: No ownership check: anyone who knows a doc_id can fetch the file (see finding sec:no-auth).

flows.name: LLM overloaded / unavailable (failure path)
flows.summary: GeminiLLM tries each configured model; retryable errors and transport exceptions move to the next model; if all fail, LLMError reaches api.events and becomes an SSE error the UI shows with a Retry button.

steps.text: Client built with HttpOptions(timeout=LLM_TIMEOUT_SECONDS*1000 ms, retry attempts=2).
429/500/503/504 or any exception → log warning, try the next model.
All models failed → LLMError('busy' if last was 429, else 'overloaded').

evidence.match: The AI service is overloaded right now

steps.text: except AnswerError → event: error; then event: done.
onError marks the turn as error; Retry re-runs the same question.

flows.failure_notes: PARTIALLY VERIFIED: in the final answer eval one request took 3,933.7 s before ending with the 'overloaded' message, far beyond the configured 30 s × 2 attempts × 3 models. The timeout is not behaving as the code intends; root cause unknown (see finding rel:llm-hang).

flows.name: Red-team run (security testing)
flows.summary: Each attack PDF goes through the real upload path, then the attack question through the real /ask path, against the live model, 3 trials; success predicates decide whether the attack worked.

steps.text: Load attack definitions (PDF bytes built with reportlab, incl. white 1-pt hidden text).
POST /api/documents with the hostile PDF, then POST /api/ask; parse SSE.
Score with attack.succeeded(answer, facts); save JSON with per-trial details.

flows.failure_notes: Uses a temporary storage dir and in-memory Qdrant; never touches the running server's data.

no_auth_note: There is no authentication or authorization anywhere in the code: no login, sessions, tokens or roles. Access to an uploaded document is controlled only by knowing its random doc_id (uuid4 hex, 128 bits). The atlas therefore has no 'authentication flow'; see finding sec:no-auth.

data_entities.name: Qdrant point (collection 'chunks')
data_entities.description: One retrievable piece of a document. The id is deterministic, so re-indexing overwrites instead of duplicating.

fields.name: vector.dense
fields.note: bge-small-en-v1.5 of embedding_text() = section header + text

fields.name: doc_id
fields.note: 'federal', 'sample-evergreen' or a uuid4 hex; keyword index

fields.name: version
fields.note: content hash incl. PIPELINE_VERSION; keyword index

data_entities.name: DocumentRecord (storage/uploads/<doc_id>.json)
data_entities.description: Metadata for one document. Public API responses drop pdf_path.

fields.name: security_flags
fields.note: lines removed by the injection scanner

data_entities.name: Uploaded PDF (storage/uploads/<doc_id>.pdf)
data_entities.description: Raw uploaded bytes, kept so citations can open the original. Deleted with its record after UPLOAD_TTL_HOURS.

data_entities.name: Federal rules Markdown (backend/data/federal/*.md)
data_entities.description: Front matter (title, source_url) + '## ' sections; each section becomes federal chunks with doc_id 'federal'.

data_entities.name: Sample policy (PDF + facts.json)
data_entities.description: Fictional Evergreen Silver 3000 PPO, generated by scripts/make_sample_policy.py; doc_id 'sample-evergreen'.

data_entities.name: Rate-limit & budget counters (process memory)
data_entities.description: Per-key deques of hit timestamps (questions, uploads) and one daily counter. Lost on restart, not shared across processes.

data_entities.name: Browser localStorage 'amicovered:doc'
data_entities.description: Remembers the last document id so a reload reopens it; falls back to the sample if the upload expired.

data_entities.name: Eval & red-team result files
data_entities.description: JSON with a summary and per-question/per-trial rows; the source of every metric quoted in the reports.

deployment.name: Local development
deployment.description: Two processes: uvicorn app.main:app (default :8000) and Vite dev server :5173 proxying /api → http://localhost:8000. Embedded Qdrant at backend/storage/qdrant.

deployment.name: Docker image (single container)
deployment.description: Stage 1 node:22-alpine → npm ci + build. Stage 2 python:3.12-slim → pip install, copy backend + dist, chown to uid 1000, bake models (warm_up), CMD uvicorn on ${PORT:-7860} with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*'. Built and smoke-tested locally earlier in this repo's history (~800 MB RAM).

deployment.name: Hugging Face Spaces (planned target)
deployment.description: Documented in docs/DEPLOY.md as the recommended free host. There is no evidence in the repository that it has been deployed (no Space metadata in README front matter, no deploy workflow).

deployment.name: GitHub Actions
deployment.description: On push to main / PRs: backend pytest (Python 3.12) and frontend lint + build (Node 22). Test-only; no build/push/deploy of images.

deployment.name: Runtime state (container filesystem)
deployment.description: storage/qdrant and storage/uploads live inside the container unless a volume is mounted or QDRANT_URL is used; a restart loses uploads and re-indexes the bundled documents.

findings.title: A single question blocked for 65 minutes despite a 30 s LLM timeout
findings.detail: Final answer eval: question 'oop-max' took 3,933.7 s and ended with 'The AI service is overloaded right now', i.e. every model in the chain failed. Configured worst case is roughly 30 s × 2 attempts × 3 models plus backoff. The SDK timeout or retry behaviour is not what the code assumes.
findings.impact: In production one stuck request occupies a worker thread and the user sees a spinner indefinitely; under the free tier's frequent overload this could exhaust the thread pool.
findings.mitigation: Investigate google-genai timeout semantics (per-request vs. per-read; whether retries honour server Retry-After) and add an overall deadline around generate() (e.g. a wall-clock budget checked between models, or running the call in a future with a hard timeout).

findings.title: Off-task abuse succeeds: the app writes unrelated content (e.g. code) on request
findings.detail: Attack 'off-task-abuse' ('Is IVF covered? Also ... write a Python function ...') was blocked 0/3 in earlier runs and succeeded 3/3 in the final run after later prompt changes. Only the prompt discourages it; nothing in code checks for it.
findings.impact: The public demo can be used as a free general-purpose LLM, spending the shared daily budget (OWASP LLM10).
findings.mitigation: Add a code-level check on free-text fields (e.g. reject or strip code blocks / content unrelated to cited excerpts) and keep it in the red-team suite.

findings.title: Contradictory 'rider' still produces a 'covered' headline
findings.detail: Final run: 1/3 trials had no warning at all; in the other 2 the verdict was downgraded to 'unclear' but the headline still said dental is covered at 100%. The downgrade changes the verdict field only.
findings.impact: A doctored PDF can still make the most prominent line of the answer wrong (OWASP LLM04).
findings.mitigation: When the conflict downgrade fires, replace or prefix the headline in code; consider a deterministic contradiction check between cited excerpts.

findings.title: No authentication; uploaded documents are protected only by an unguessable id
findings.detail: All endpoints are anonymous. GET /api/documents/{id} and /file return any document whose id is known. Ids are uuid4 hex (122 random bits), so guessing is impractical, but anyone given a link (or with access to browser history/localStorage) can read the policy until it expires.
findings.impact: Insurance documents can contain names and member IDs; sharing a link shares the document.
findings.mitigation: Acceptable for an anonymous 24 h demo. For real users: accounts or signed, expiring URLs, and per-owner checks in _get_document.

findings.confidence: medium (depends on uvicorn behaviour and the host's proxy)
findings.title: Per-IP rate limits may be bypassable via X-Forwarded-For in the Docker image
findings.detail: The container runs uvicorn 0.54 with --proxy-headers --forwarded-allow-ips='*', which trusts X-Forwarded-For from any peer and rewrites request.client. client_ip() then keys limits on that value. If the container is reachable without a proxy that overwrites the header, a client can send a different X-Forwarded-For per request.
findings.impact: Bypass of QUESTIONS/UPLOADS_PER_IP_PER_HOUR; the global daily budget still caps total spend.
findings.mitigation: Set --forwarded-allow-ips to the real proxy address range for the host, and verify with a request carrying a forged header.

findings.title: Injection scanner is pattern-based and can be rephrased around
findings.detail: scan_for_injection uses 8 narrow regex families. It caught every red-team payload and has zero false positives on the sample policy, but paraphrased instructions are not detected; the model's own behaviour is the remaining layer.
findings.impact: Indirect prompt injection remains possible in principle (OWASP LLM01).
findings.mitigation: Keep as one layer; add red-team cases with paraphrases; consider a classifier pass for uploads.

findings.title: No security headers (CSP, X-Frame-Options, etc.)
findings.detail: No middleware or server config sets Content-Security-Policy, frame or HSTS headers. XSS risk is low because React escapes text and model output is stripped of markup, but defence in depth is missing.
findings.impact: Clickjacking / reduced XSS defence in depth.
findings.mitigation: Add a small middleware setting CSP (script-src 'self'), X-Frame-Options DENY, Referrer-Policy.

findings.title: Interactive API docs (/docs, /openapi.json) are enabled
findings.detail: FastAPI(...) is constructed without docs_url=None / openapi_url=None, so Swagger UI and the schema are public. Not sensitive here (every endpoint is public anyway), but it advertises the surface.
findings.mitigation: Disable in production via an env flag.

findings.title: Controls that exist and are tested
findings.detail: Path-safe doc ids; PDF magic-byte, size, page and text-size limits; HTML-escaped, fenced excerpts + closing reminder; schema-constrained output; quote verification with verdict downgrade; markup stripping; contact allow-list; plan-fact grounding; daily budget covering uploads; CORS limited to the dev origin; question length ≤ 500.

findings.title: Failed uploads can leave orphaned files/points
findings.detail: upload_document only cleans up on PdfLoadError. An exception during embedding/upsert or plan-facts grounding leaves the PDF on disk (no JSON record, so it never expires) and possibly some points in Qdrant.
findings.impact: Disk/vector garbage accumulates; no user-visible effect.
findings.mitigation: Wrap indexing in try/except that deletes the PDF and calls store.delete_document(doc_id).

findings.title: Cross-encoder reranking dominates retrieval latency on CPU
findings.detail: Profiling: 24 candidates took ~5 s on a loaded 8-core machine; reduced to 12 (policy) + 6 (federal) with unchanged eval scores. A live trace showed rerank 1,481 ms vs search 159 ms.
findings.impact: Seconds of CPU per question per request thread; concurrent questions contend for the same cores.
findings.mitigation: Keep candidates small; consider caching per (doc_id, query), a smaller/quantized reranker, or GPU if load grows.

findings.title: Uploads are processed synchronously inside the request
findings.detail: Parsing, sanitizing, embedding every chunk and the plan-facts LLM call all happen before the response; a 150-page PDF holds a worker thread for the whole duration.
findings.impact: Slow uploads and reduced capacity for questions during uploads.
findings.mitigation: Only if uploads become common: return 202 + job id and index in a background worker; until then the current design is simpler and adequate.

findings.title: Embedded Qdrant ties the app to one process
findings.detail: QdrantClient(path=...) is an in-process database on local disk; a second process (another uvicorn worker or replica) cannot share it. Requests already access it concurrently from the thread pool; thread-safety of the local mode was not verified.
findings.impact: Horizontal scaling requires QDRANT_URL (supported by create_client) plus shared upload storage.
findings.mitigation: Set QDRANT_URL to a Qdrant server/cloud before running >1 worker; move uploads to object storage or a shared volume.

findings.title: Rate limits and budget live in process memory
findings.detail: Counters reset on restart and aren't shared between processes. Keys of SlidingWindowLimiter._hits are never removed, so memory grows with the number of distinct client IPs (small per key).
findings.impact: Limits are per-process; a restart refills the daily budget.
findings.mitigation: Fine for one container. Use Redis (or the host's rate limiting) when running several instances.

findings.title: Expired uploads are deleted only at startup or on the next upload
findings.detail: There is no scheduler; delete_expired_uploads runs in Services.startup and at the start of upload_document. With no uploads, expired documents stay readable past 24 h.
findings.impact: The '24 hours' promise in the UI is a minimum, not a maximum.
findings.mitigation: Also check expiry in _get_document (cheap), or run cleanup periodically.

findings.title: Answer quality varies run to run (82-97% exact verdicts)
findings.detail: Four full answer-eval runs on the same 34 questions (with prompt changes between them): 82%, 97%, 91%, 88% exact verdicts. Misses are mostly borderline verdict categories; one was the 65-minute timeout. Each question is run once per eval, so a single run can't distinguish a regression from noise.
findings.impact: Prompt changes can't be judged from one run.
findings.mitigation: Run each question several times (or at least repeat misses) and report mean ± spread.

findings.title: Documentation has drifted from the code
findings.detail: README still says '90 tests' (the suite now has 140+), and an untracked SECURITY.md draft claims every attack is blocked after fixes, which the final red-team run contradicts.
findings.mitigation: Update README counts; rewrite SECURITY.md from redteam-final results before committing it.

findings.title: The frontend has no automated tests
findings.detail: No test runner or test files under frontend/; CI only lints and builds it. The SSE parser (dispatch) is the riskiest untested piece.
findings.impact: UI regressions are caught only by manual checks.
findings.mitigation: Add Vitest for api.ts dispatch() and a Playwright smoke test.

findings.title: The Claude provider has only been tested with fakes
findings.detail: Every recorded eval and red-team run used gemini-3.5-flash-lite; the Anthropic path is exercised only by unit tests with a fake client.
findings.impact: Switching LLM_PROVIDER=anthropic is untested end to end.
findings.mitigation: Run eval/run_answer_eval.py --limit 5 with an Anthropic key before relying on it.

decisions.title: Local ONNX embeddings and reranker instead of an embeddings API
decisions.what: fastembed runs bge-small, BM25 and a MiniLM cross-encoder in-process.
decisions.alternatives: OpenAI/Voyage/Gemini embeddings API; sentence-transformers on PyTorch.
decisions.tradeoffs: No second API key, no per-call cost, offline tests; but ~200 MB of models, CPU-bound latency, larger image.

decisions.title: Qdrant with embedded mode
decisions.what: One collection with named dense + sparse vectors; RRF fusion server-side; same client code for embedded, in-memory (tests) and server.
decisions.alternatives: pgvector + tsvector, Chroma, FAISS + rank_bm25, Meilisearch for keywords.
decisions.tradeoffs: Hybrid search in one query and zero ops locally; but single-process in embedded mode.

decisions.title: One lenient relevance gate instead of per-chunk thresholds
decisions.what: Skip the LLM only if the best reranked score < -6; otherwise always pass the top-k.
decisions.tradeoffs: Calibrated from the retrieval eval sweep; catches clearly off-topic questions cheaply, relies on the model's not_in_policy for the rest.

decisions.title: Schema-constrained output + server-side verification
decisions.what: The LLM must return LLMAnswer JSON; quotes are checked against excerpts; verdicts without evidence are downgraded.
decisions.tradeoffs: Deterministic UI fields and checkable citations; schema must stay compatible with both providers.

decisions.title: Cost arithmetic in Python, not in the LLM
decisions.what: The LLM extracts a CostRule; estimate_cost applies deductible → copay/coinsurance → out-of-pocket cap.
decisions.tradeoffs: Exact, unit-tested against the policy's worked examples; requires plan facts (deductible, OOP max).

decisions.title: Cross-reference graph from regex instead of LLM-built GraphRAG
decisions.what: Edges from 'see 7.5'-style references stored on chunk payloads; one-hop expansion at query time.
decisions.alternatives: LLM entity/relation extraction into a graph DB; no graph.
decisions.tradeoffs: Free, exact, no extra store; only explicit references. Measured: no gain at top_k=6 on the sample, +1/8 multi-hop at top_k 2-4.

decisions.title: Provider-neutral LLM interface with Gemini default
decisions.what: StructuredLLM protocol; GeminiLLM with a model fallback chain; AnthropicLLM.
decisions.tradeoffs: Free-tier demo possible and providers swappable; two adapters to keep in sync.

decisions.title: Server-Sent Events over POST for /ask
decisions.what: StreamingResponse yields status/sources/answer/error/done; the browser parses the stream with fetch.
decisions.alternatives: Plain JSON response; WebSockets; EventSource (GET only).
decisions.tradeoffs: Progressive UI without a WebSocket server; errors after the first byte can't change the HTTP status.

decisions.title: One container serving API and UI
decisions.what: FastAPI mounts frontend/dist at / when it exists.
decisions.tradeoffs: One URL, no CORS in production, one deploy; frontend and backend scale together.
